issues.title: ICE building `glam`: Projecting into SIMD type std::arch::aarch64::float32x4_t is banned by MCP#838

processing.reason: The PR's historical defect is a MIR-validation failure, not a value-level miscompilation. Before the fix, SROA failed to mark #[repr(simd)] ADTs as escaping, scalar-replaced an unused/field-only SIMD local into field projections, and thus emitted MIR that projects into a SIMD type—rejected by the MCP#838 validator (the rust-lang/rust#144621 ICE). The corrected behavior merely preserves the SIMD local whole. The supplied regression is a MIR optimization test, not an execution test, and the decoded before/after MIR shows no value change. Constructing two ordinary Rust functions with different defined outputs would require an unrelated semantic change (e.g., arbitrary array-index or return-value differences), which the task forbids. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair with differing defined values exists for this bug.

analysis.originalLogic: In `escaping_locals`, the pre-fix escape test only special-cased the `DynMetadata` lang item: `if let ty::Adt(def, _args) = ty.kind()` followed by `&& tcx.is_lang_item(def.did(), LangItem::DynMetadata)`. That branch returned `true` so codegen would see `DynMetadata<T>` rather than an inner reference-to-opaque type. Other ADTs, including `#[repr(simd)]` SIMD types, were not forced to escape, so SRoA could treat their uses as replaceable fields.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The old SRoA escape analysis failed to mark a `#[repr(simd)]` ADT local as escaping, allowing the pass to scalar-replace/expand the SIMD aggregate into array-like storage or field projections. The patch describes this as SIMD types being "de-optimized into an array" when "the value is unused" and the pass "sees \"all the uses are of the fields\" and expands it." Such projections into SIMD types are forbidden by MCP#838; the linked bug reports the validator error "Projecting into SIMD type std::arch::aarch64::float32x4_t is banned by MCP#838". The corrected transformation is to return `true` from `escaping_locals` for SIMD ADTs, preserving the SIMD local instead of expanding it.
analysis.inputDomain: Optimized MIR for functions containing locals whose type is an ADT with `def.repr().simd()` true, especially `std::simd::Simd<u8, 16>` under `#![feature(portable_simd)]` and architecture SIMD types such as `std::arch::aarch64::float32x4_t`. Relevant locals include unused SIMD parameters and SIMD values whose only apparent uses are field projections, since those are the cases where SRoA previously considered expansion valid. The regression test's function signature is `pub(crate) fn foo(simds: &[Simd<u8, 16>], _unused: Simd<u8, 16>)` and reads `simds[0]`; the test is a MIR optimization test, not an execution test.
analysis.summary: Historical bug fix: ScalarReplacementOfAggregates must not scalar-replace `#[repr(simd)]` ADT locals. The escape analysis previously special-cased only `DynMetadata`; the fix also marks SIMD ADTs as escaping, preventing de-optimization into arrays and illegal projections into SIMD types banned by MCP#838.
analysis.trigger: Trigger when SRoA examines a local whose type is a SIMD ADT, such as an unused `Simd<u8, 16>` parameter or a SIMD value with only field uses. Under the old guard, only `DynMetadata` was forced to escape; the SIMD ADT therefore remained eligible and the pass expanded it. The fix adds `def.repr().simd()` to the escape condition so the SIMD local is retained.
preconditions: The function is compiled through MIR optimization including `ScalarReplacementOfAggregates`.
A local has an ADT type for which `def.repr().simd()` is true, e.g. `std::simd::Simd<u8, 16>` or an architecture SIMD type.
The SIMD local is unused or has only field-like uses that make SRoA consider aggregate expansion, as described by the patch comment.
The compiler invariant from MCP#838 must hold: projecting into a SIMD type is banned.
pitfalls: The guard applies to ADTs with `def.repr().simd()`, not to ordinary arrays such as `[T; N]`; do not broaden the condition to all aggregates.
An unused SIMD local is still a trigger: the patch comment says expansion happens when the value is unused because the pass sees all uses as fields.
The new condition is an OR with the existing `DynMetadata` check, so the `DynMetadata` behavior must remain intact.

The supplied regression `.diff` shows the fixed before/after MIR both preserving `std::simd::Simd<u8, 16>`; it should not be read as the historical wrong output. The historical wrong rewrite is described by the source comment and the linked ICE report.
Do not claim the ICE was reproduced locally: the evidence here is the source patch, test expectations, and issue text.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt/sroa` MIR test with `#![feature(portable_simd)]` and a function taking a slice of `Simd<u8, 16>` plus an unused SIMD parameter. Emit `ScalarReplacementOfAggregates` MIR and use FileCheck to reject `[u8; 16]` around the relevant local and assignment, while requiring the SIMD local declaration and the element copy. The supplied test uses `pub(crate) fn foo(simds: &[Simd<u8, 16>], _unused: Simd<u8, 16>)`, `// CHECK-NOT: [u8; 16]`, `// CHECK: let [[SIMD:_.+]]: std::simd::Simd<u8, 16>;`, and `// CHECK: [[SIMD]] = copy (*_1)[0 of 1];`. Include `//@ needs-unwind` because the generated MIR has an unwind continuation. This verifies the corrected MIR transformation without executing the program.
evidence: // Exclude #[repr(simd)] types so that they are not de-optimized into an array
// (MCP#838 banned projections into SIMD types, but if the value is unused
// this pass sees "all the uses are of the fields" and expands it.)
